purpose: Test the shortcut {0,3}={0,1,3} intersection {0,2,3}: represent the two tractable relaxations as projected linear delta-matroids and invoke polynomial linear-delta-matroid intersection.
source_alignment: Koana-Wahlstrom: every projected linear delta-matroid admits an elementary projection representation from a linear delta-matroid; every linear delta-matroid is even.
Shao-Zivny: arity-3 degree constraints with gaps of length at most one are symmetric delta-matroids; matching-realizable constraints have all gaps of the same length 0 or 1.

theorem.name: R1_R2_NOT_PROJECTED_LINEAR_OVER_ANY_FIELD_V1_7
theorem.statement: Neither R1 nor R2 is a projected linear delta-matroid over any field in the skew-symmetric representation used by linear delta-matroid intersection.
proof_R1: If R1 were projected linear, elementary projection gives a linear delta-matroid L on {a,b,c,h} whose projection deleting h is exactly R1.

L is even, so for each visible feasible F exactly one of F and F union {h} can be feasible, determined by the common parity. Twisting by {h} if needed reduces to the even lift L={empty,{a,h},{b,h},{c,h},{a,b,c,h}}.
Because empty is feasible, L is directly represented by a 4x4 skew-symmetric matrix A.
Feasibility of {a,h},{b,h},{c,h} forces A_ah,A_bh,A_ch nonzero. Infeasibility of {a,b},{a,c},{b,c} forces A_ab=A_ac=A_bc=0.
But Pf(A)=A_ab*A_ch-A_ac*A_bh+A_ah*A_bc=0, so the full set cannot be feasible, contradiction.
proof_R2: The same parity normalization yields the even lift L={empty,{a,b},{a,c},{b,c},{a,b,c,h}}.
Direct representation forces A_ab,A_ac,A_bc nonzero and A_ah=A_bh=A_ch=0.
Again Pf(A)=A_ab*A_ch-A_ac*A_bh+A_ah*A_bc=0, contradicting feasibility of the full set.

killed: Direct Koana-Wahlstrom projected-linear intersection of the two local relaxations {0,1,3} and {0,2,3}
Any claim that the local relaxation relations themselves already lie in the projected-linear class
not_killed: A nonlocal global representation that is not assembled by replacing each {0,3} vertex independently by R1/R2 projected-linear gadgets
Perfect matching with the exact GF(2) all-or-none constraints enforced globally
A new augmentation theorem specialized to simultaneous {0,3} defects

next_target.name: E8_GLOBAL_GF2_CONSTRAINED_MATCHING_OR_AUGMENTATION_V1_8
next_target.directive: Encode the tractable clause/inverter side by matching/general-factor machinery and retain each variable all-or-none constraint as the two GF(2) equations e1+e2=0 and e2+e3=0. Seek a polynomial global algorithm for perfect/general matching under exactly these disjoint rank-2 parity constraints. Reject group-algebra/Fourier methods with dimension 2^n or any local relaxation that admits false positives.
